title: Heightmap-gradient particle filter on real Copernicus DEM (SPRIN-D CTU method) vs TERCOM
summary: Re-implementation of the CTU SPRIN-D winner's localization (arXiv 2510.01348): local heightmap gradients matched to a prior DEM with the unnormalized correlation coefficient, Gaussian-blurred similarity maps weighting a translational particle filter resampled every fixed odometry distance, K-means largest-cluster estimate. Runs 10 km simulated flights with VIO-like drift over three real Copernicus GLO-30 windows (Bavarian Forest hills, Erding where SPRIN-D was flown, Hungarian plain) plus a smoothed-flat control, and compares against a radar-altimeter batch TERCOM baseline. Reports error vs distance, convergence from a 300 m initial offset, flat-terrain failure, a sensor-error sweep and measured CPU time per update.
verified: ran 2026-11-06 with CPython 3.13.15 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 / rasterio 1.5.2 / matplotlib 3.11.2 on an Apple M2 Max: fetch_dem.py downloaded the three GLO-30 windows over public HTTPS, run_eval.py produced every number and plot in README (results deterministic across two full runs, timings vary with machine load), test_core.py 14 passed and fails when the correlation flip or similarity-map origin is mutated. The flights, odometry and heightmap sensor are simulated; no real UAV, LiDAR or SfM data was used. The paper's own numbers are quoted from the paper, not reproduced.
